Bang Blinding Index

Source: R/blinding.R
blindingIndex.Rd

Computes Bang's arm-specific blinding index and normal-approximation confidence interval. A guess matching the actual arm is correct; dont_know is neutral; any other value, including an unknown arm label or missing guess, is incorrect.

Usage

blindingIndex(
  guesses,
  arm_col = "arm",
  guess_col = "guess",
  dont_know = "dont_know",
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

guesses

Data frame containing actual assignments and guesses.

arm_col

Name of the actual-assignment column.

guess_col

Name of the guess column.

dont_know

Sentinel used for a "don't know" response.

conf_level

Confidence level strictly between zero and one.

Value

A blinding_index object.

References

Bang H, Ni L, Davis CE (2004). Assessment of blinding in clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 25, 143-156.

Examples

guesses <- data.frame(
  arm = c("active", "active", "control", "control"),
  guess = c("active", "dont_know", "active", "control")
)
blindingIndex(guesses)
#> Bang blinding index (95% confidence interval)
#>      arm n n_correct n_incorrect n_dontknow  BI        SE   ci_lower ci_upper
#>   active 2         1           0          1 0.5 0.3535534 -0.1929519 1.192952
#>  control 2         1           1          0 0.0 0.7071068 -1.3859038 1.385904
